comment: Vendored half of a cross-language contract. Each fixture carries the rules it asserts, written so a second implementation can be coded from the file alone; this directory is that second implementation's anchor. The bytes here are deliberately NOT generated from the kernel: they are a copy pinned by sha256, so a change to the published contract shows up here as a red hash check rather than as a silent re-generation. test_kernel_fixtures.py enforces (1) vendor == manifest, (2) every entry names a consumer test that exists, (3) when KERNEL_FIXTURES_DIR points at a live kernel checkout, its bytes must match the pin too. Update procedure: bump kernel, npm pack iterate-kernel@<new>, copy the file, re-record sha256 here, then the consumer test must still pass — if it does not, the two implementations genuinely diverge and the kernel change is the bug, not this file.
